newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Assassin says bomb intended for SAfrican communist.
newsitem.headline: Assassin says bomb intended for SAfrican communist.

text.p: Convicted state assassin Eugene de Kock said on Monday a parcel bomb which killed anti-apartheid activist Ruth First in 1982 had been intended for her husband, South African communist leader Joe Slovo.

De Kock, who has blown the lid on dirty tricks committed or sanctioned by high-ranking apartheid security officers, cabinet ministers and presidents during his plea for leniency on six murder charges, said a sergeant told him about the bomb in 1985.

"What I heard was that the bomb was for Joe Slovo. They (the couple) worked at the same university in Maputo (Mozambique). She opened the bomb instead of Slovo," de Kock told the Pretoria Supreme Courts. He did not say who sent the bomb.
As chief of staff of the military wing of Nelson Mandela's African National Congress (ANC) and secretary general of the South African Communist Party, Slovo survived several attempts on his life.
He died of cancer last year while serving in Mandela's cabinet as housing minister, having returned to South Africa in 1990 after the unbanning of the ANC and Mandela's release from prison.
